pride-lodge.title: Pride Lodge, Blackpool: gay guest house
pride-lodge.description: Pride Lodge on High Street is a mixed LGBTQ+ guest house with sauna, gym and seasonal hot tub, a minute from the Flying Handbag. Plan your stay.
pride-lodge.h1: Staying at Pride Lodge: a welcoming gay guest house by Blackpool North
pride-lodge.intro: Pride Lodge is a small LGBTQ+ guest house on High Street that welcomes everyone, with its own sauna and gym and a short stroll to the main bars.
pride-lodge.body_html:
Who is Pride Lodge best for?

Pride Lodge works well if you want a gay-run base that is relaxed rather than rowdy. It describes itself as mixed rather than men-only, so it suits couples, friends travelling together and anyone who would rather not stay above a bar.

It sits in the older guest-house streets between the station and Dickson Road, which makes arrival easy: you can walk from the train. If this is your first Blackpool gay weekend, this is a low-stress place to start.

Rooms and facilities

Rooms come with a smart TV, a fridge and a light breakfast served in the room. The extras are what set it apart:

  • Sauna, sunbed and multi-gym for guests
  • Garden hot tub in season, roughly April to early October
  • Discount card for local venues and standing tickets for Funny Girls
  • Discounted passes for the Banks Street car park, sold at reception

Is Pride Lodge men-only or adults-only?

Neither is stated: it calls itself a mixed LGBTQ+ guest house and everyone is welcome. Our research could not confirm an adults-only rule, so ask when you book if you are travelling with children.

Your nearest options from Pride Lodge:

  • Rendezvous Bar and Rooms, 1 min away: a small, friendly bar with rooms at the station end of Lord Street.
  • The Flying Handbag, 1 min away: a big Queen Street bar and club with drag hosts, karaoke and a sun terrace.
  • Funny Girls, 2 mins away: drag cabaret in a restored art deco cinema, with listed show nights Wednesday to Sunday.

Hours change, so see what is open tonight before you head out. For the full venue background, see the Rainbow Quarter directory.

Getting there and getting around

From Blackpool North it is about 1 min on foot, so you can arrive by train and be checked in quickly. The Prom at North Pier is 9 mins away and the Tower is 12 mins, so a sea-air stroll before dinner is easy to fit in. The safety guide has sensible tips for getting home after dark.

Is it the right fit?

A mixed LGBTQ+ stay is the easiest option for friends who want a welcoming base without a single rule for everyone. If Pride Lodge is full or not quite right, the nearest alternatives by walking time are Q Accommodation, Mardi Gras, Trades Hotel and Bar; the stays directory compares them all.

Booking tips

Pride Lodge has a three-night minimum on event weekends and offers money off Sunday-to-Thursday stays of two nights or more. Reception is staffed 10am to 7pm Monday to Saturday and 11am to 5pm Sunday, with WhatsApp out of hours, so message ahead if you will arrive late.

Rooms go early for Blackpool Pride and the Illuminations, so book as soon as you know your dates. Prices and availability change, so always check the venue's own site or phone before you pay: https://www.pridelodge.com/.

Good to know

  • Reception is on listed hours, so tell them your arrival time
  • Buy your parking pass at reception before you park
  • Sauna, gym and hot tub details come from the owner-checked listing; confirm what is open when you book
  • Our extra research could not independently verify the facilities, so check the guest house site

  • Sunday roasts, which you need to book
